text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually has no symptoms, which is why it is often called the "silent killer". Most people feel completely fine even if their blood pressure is dangerously high.
You generally will not notice signs unless your blood pressure spikes very high or reaches a dangerous crisis level. Potential signs include:

list.snippet: Early-morning headaches (especially dull pain at the back of the head)
Blurred vision or blood spots in the eyes
Shortness of breath (especially with light activity)
Pounding or throbbing sensation in the ears, neck, or chest

text_blocks.snippet: A blood pressure reading of 180/120 mm Hg or higher is a medical emergency. Call 911 immediately if these high readings happen alongside any of these warning signs:

list.snippet: Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath
Numbness, weakness, or signs of a stroke (such as facial drooping or slurred speech)

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about official blood pressure categories and guidance from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention or review detailed overviews via the Mayo Clinic.
